plan: My private value is $24. In a second-price sealed auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $24 ensures I only win if the item is worth more to me than what others will pay. If I win, I'll pay less than my bid. If I bid less, I risk losing an item that could generate profit. With no prior auction history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid is most rational.

My private value is $16. This means I'll profit if I win the item for less than $16. My optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. Since values are drawn randomly and independently, I'll bid strategically around my value. I'll choose a bid that gives me a good chance of winning without overpaying. A bid of $15.5 seems reasonable - close to my value but with some buffer for potential profit.
